alex_reyes: heads-up — after the runtime deploy at 09:12 we're seeing p99 latency spikes specifically for seq lengths ~512-1024. looks like KV hit rate for those bins dropped ~35%

sasha_ng: confirmed on prod-dashboard. interestingly p50/p95 fine, so probably cache churn or a keying mismatch, not batching degredation :thinking_face:

juan_perez: i pulled a few traces, two patterns: 1) driver restarts right before spike windows, 2) keys coming from older model variants that don't match new namespace prefix. sample from logs: `kv.get("m-v1|sbin=3|sid=...") -> miss` then `kv.populate(..., key="m-v2|sbin=3|sid=...")` so same seqlen bin ends up double-writing under different prefixes

olivia_bot: deploy-bot: deployment "runtime-arch-3" finished at 09:11:48. rollout: 100%

alex_reyes: here's a tiny repro snippet i used locally to simulate churn:
```python
# simulate two driver versions writing different prefixes
old_key = f"{model}:v1:sb{seq_bin}:{sess}"
new_key = f"{model}:v2:sb{seq_bin}:{sess}"
kv.set(old_key, some_kv)
# restart driver, new instance writes new_key on populate
```

tara_choi: if keys are namespace-prefixed by driver_version, we need a migration or backward-compatible lookup. we shouldn't invalidate existing entries on minor driver bumps. maybe lookup fallback: try new prefix, then old prefix for X minutes

juan_perez: fallback idea ok but we saw a pathological case where fallback doubled cache writes and evicted hotter entries in sbin=3. causing more misses. fallback must be read-only (try old keys) and only populate under the canonical/current prefix

alex_reyes: agreed. proposal: 1) add a short lived multi-lookup read path: try current prefix -> if miss try last-stable-prefix (no populate) -> serve if hit. 2) emit metric kv.fallback_hits and kv.fallback_reads to monitor. 3) queue a migration job that rekeys old entries into current namespace in background (rate limited)

sasha_ng: sounds good. quick mitigation: rollback runtime-arch-3 to previous binary for Canary nodes while we test fallback read path in staging

tara_choi: on the persistence side, i think we should version the key schema and store a compact "key_version" in the value metadata. that way the lookup layer can pick the right decode/rehash behavior. also limits accidental double-writes when shape changes

juan_perez: true. plus add seqlen-bin affinity tags so eviction considers cross-bin hotness. right now eviction is global LRU which hurts mid-range bins when there's clustered traffic

alex_reyes: short runbook for oncall: 1) if p99 spike, check kv.hit_ratio by sbin (grafana panel) 2) if sbin drop and driver restarts correlate, rollback to runtime-arch-2 3) enable temporary canary fallback read via flag `kv.read_fallback=true` 4) watch kv.fallback_hits > 0 to ensure we're catching the old keys

olivia_bot: alert: kv.hit_ratio.sbin3 dropped 38% (09:14 -> 09:18). rolling back canary group in 2m

alex_reyes: follow-ups: - PR to implement read-fallback (no populate) + metrics - small migration tool to rekey old->current with throttling - longer-term: canonical key format with semantic version in prefix so minor driver changes don't create incompatible namespaces

tara_choi: i'll draft the PR for read-fallback and metric names. can we use existing counter names: `kv.fallback_reads`, `kv.fallback_hits`, `kv.rekeys_migrated`?

juan_perez: yes those names are fine. i'll own the migration tool (rate limit via tokens/sec) and add tests that simulate interleaved writes across versions

sasha_ng: i'll coordinate rollback on canaries and prepare a staging cut where we test fallback and migration with synthetic traffic for sbin=3 and sbin=4

alex_reyes: thanks. quick bench: with fallback read-only lookups added, estimated p99 improvement for sbin3 is ~14% (based on local replay). will post numbers after staging run

tara_choi: flagged for eng-runtime sprint: add key_version + seqlen_affinity to schema. also add eviction policy experiment: per-bin LRU quota

juan_perez: note: when we do migration, lock-free rekeying only (read old, write new) and set TTL small for legacy keys to avoid indefinite duplication

alex_reyes: perfect. logging note — include `orig_prefix` in kv.populate logs so we can audit how many stems came from older prefixes

sasha_ng: yup. i'll update the runbook and notify infra on the rollback window. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
